title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Stocks fell Tuesday (Dow -0.6%, S&P -0.5%, Nasdaq -0.8%) as the 10-year Treasury yield spiked to 5.04% - highest since 2007 - with futures pointing lower again ahead of today's Fed decision.

Markets: Brent crude jumped ~2% to top $108/bbl after Saudi Arabia shut its key East-West pipeline following drone attacks; Chevron's CEO warned global oil supply is running low with no relief in sight.
Markets: Crypto slid after the Senate blocked the industry's CLARITY Act in a procedural vote - Bitcoin fell ~4% below $76,000 and Coinbase dropped 10%.

Companies: AI leaders (Anthropic's Amodei, OpenAI's Altman, Musk) called for slowing frontier AI development on safety grounds over the weekend; Nvidia's Huang pushed back and Trump dismissed the warnings as a 'hoax,' while cybersecurity stocks (CrowdStrike +14%) rallied on AI-cyberattack fears.

Companies: Dreamforce in San Francisco becomes ground zero for the AI-pace debate as Nvidia, OpenAI and Anthropic CEOs converge; Anthropic is still expected to file for a mega-IPO (~$100B raise, ~$2T valuation) despite the safety rhetoric.

Macro/Policy: The Fed's rate decision lands today at 2pm ET under new Chair Kevin Warsh, with markets seeing real odds of the first hike since 2023 as oil-driven inflation and AI power demand complicate the outlook.

Macro/Policy: US diesel hit a record $6.27/gallon (AAA) amid global refining constraints; EPA also finalized repeal of Biden-era power-plant CO2 rules, a move with stakes for a pending Supreme Court case.
